rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: BoE Nov 5 hike to 4.00% ~97% (7–2 vote expected); Fed Dec hike ~81% (from ~83%); ECB Dec ~89%; BoJ Dec ~80%; BoC Dec ~56%; RBA hiked to 4.85% Nov 3
rows.read: Most big central banks still lean toward higher rates, and the Bank of England is set to raise on Thursday. Bank of Japan minutes backed more rises, and bets on a December Fed hike barely moved after the US elections. Currencies now move on hints about the next step, not on hikes already expected.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Australia trade surplus A$2.8B Sep (7-month high); US ADP +86K (fcst +67K); ISM services 54.5 (fcst 54.8); US jobless claims fcst 197K
rows.read: Australia's exports rose strongly, giving it its biggest trade surplus in seven months. US figures this week have been mixed but healthy, and a Democratic Congress is expected to spend less, which could slow US growth next year. US jobs figures on Thursday and Friday are the next real read.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Brent ~$93.65 (4th daily fall; Wed settle $94.62, −8.7%); euro-area flash CPI 4.0% Oct; Swiss CPI 1.5% Oct; ISM services prices paid ~73
rows.read: Oil's slide on hopes of an end to the Iran war, if it lasts, would ease price pressure almost everywhere and take some heat off central banks. For now inflation is still high in the US, the UK and the euro area, so the hikes already planned stay on track.

rows.figure: Kospi lower on chip selling; USD/JPY 158.25; USD/CHF 0.8140; AUD/USD 0.7010; gold ~$4,135 (+1.9%)

rows.figure: Brent ~$93.65, WTI ~$86.98 in Asia; lowest since Aug 31; Australia trade surplus A$2.8B Sep
rows.read: Oil fell for a fourth day on bets the Iran war winds down, cutting the energy bill for importers like Japan and the euro area. Exporters like Canada and Australia earn less, though Australia's latest trade figures still showed strong gas and metals sales.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: Democrats win House and Senate (AP, Nov 3–4); Treasury refunding $125B, unchanged; Canada budget Nov 5, 3:00 PM CT; Fitch France A+ negative (Oct 30)
rows.read: Democrats now control both houses of Congress, so President Trump's spending plans look harder to pass, which takes some support away from the dollar. Canada presents its federal budget on Thursday afternoon, and France's debt worries still weigh on the euro.
